notes: QA2 scored by adapting the rubric (QRNG has no qubits/depth); override to NA if the survey prefers. Surprising, and important for how a survey summarizes it: the attack as implemented does not need to predict MT19937. The compromised sampler simply returns a crafted u* (App. A, 'directly instruments the PRNG module'), so the same supply-chain attacker could substitute the QRNG values, which are pre-generated, stored on disk and memory-mapped. The 0/100 defense result therefore reflects an attacker that hooks only the PRNG call. The paper makes exactly this argument against CSPRNGs ('a compromised CSPRNG call returns attacker-controlled values') but not for its own software-read QRNG buffer, while claiming 'information-theoretically secure' and 'unconditional security'. It also says success drops to ~1/V (Sec. 2.3) while App. B says it equals the natural token probability p_t*. The 99.6-100% attack success is near-tautological for inverse-CDF sampling. Abstract reports +0.6% median latency, but P95 latency rises 59.4%. Table 2 lists GPT-2 at 180 trials/100% vs 540 trials/99.6% in Table 1.

Defense: separate 100-trial benchmark; 50M float64 QRNG samples (400 MB) memory-mapped; latency over 1,000 iterations; chi-square test over 10^6 samples.
